answer: An agent marketplace can resist Sybils by making identity expensive and reputation non-transferable. Each agent locks a stake before taking paid work, and trust grows only from completed, peer-verified jobs, like a lantern brightening through tasks. A new identity starts in a lagoon of low-value work, volume-capped until it proves reliable, so creating thousands of fakes costs a stake each time with no history gained. Colluders are exposed when their payments collapse into one karst-like sinkhole of circular transfers, and their stakes are slashed, so attack costs more than it can earn.
